title: Excitation spectra and rank tomography of linear matrix product tangent spaces
authors: Otto T. P. Schmidt, Iacopo Carusotto
abstract: We formulate a tangent-space method for algebraic varieties of matrix product states (MPS) to study excitation spectra of non-uniform quantum many-body systems with open boundary conditions. We further introduce a rank tomography of the MPS tangent space, which characterizes its expressivity in terms of particle-sector rank profiles of the underlying MPS variety. Using the Bose--Hubbard model as a benchmark, we illustrate that the method reproduces low-lying excitations and captures finite-size precursors of the Mott-insulator to superfluid transition.
summary: The paper introduces a sophisticated geometric framework to study quantum many-body dynamics by treating the space of Matrix Product States as an algebraic variety. It develops a 'rank tomography' tool using particle-resolved rank profiles, which refines the characterization of system expressivity beyond simple bond dimensions. This method is successfully applied to approximate excitation spectra for models like the Bose-Hubbard model.
main_problem: To develop a rigorous method using tangent spaces on the manifold of Matrix Product States (MPS) to accurately calculate the low-lying excitation spectra of quantum many-body systems with open boundary conditions.
main_result: The proposed tangent-space and rank tomography methods successfully reproduce known low-energy excitations for benchmark models like the Bose-Hubbard model, providing a geometrically grounded way to approximate dynamics within constrained variational spaces.
method: The authors formulate the problem by defining the MPS space as an algebraic variety and projecting the time evolution onto its tangent space. They introduce 'rank tomography' using Particle-Resolved Schmidt Rank Profiles (PRSR) to characterize the expressivity of this manifold.
model_or_system: The primary application is to quantum many-body systems, benchmarked by the Bose-Hubbard model Hamiltonian ($H = -J \sum (\dots) + U \sum n(n-1) - \mu \sum n$). The analysis focuses on truncating the local Hilbert space (e.g., $n_i=0, 1, 2$) and treating the state within the MPS variational manifold.
key_observables: Excitation spectra ($\omega$), Particle-Resolved Schmidt Rank Profile (PRSR), and the generalized eigenvalue problem solutions derived from projecting dynamics onto the horizontal tangent space.
important_parameters: Hopping amplitude ($J$), on-site interaction ($U$), chemical potential ($\mu$), and bond dimensions ($D$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on approximating the true spectrum by diagonalizing an effective Hamiltonian projected onto the tangent space, which is derived from enforcing the Dirac-Frenkel condition. The analysis also assumes specific smoothness properties of related algebraic varieties.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the MPS representation in a left-canonical gauge; Figure 3 compares the exact and reconstructed low-energy spectra for the Bose-Hubbard model, showing agreement between methods.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the geometric framework by defining the MPS space as an algebraic variety and proving its smoothness. It then develops the tangent-space projection method (TDVP) to derive a reduced eigenvalue problem ($	ext{Bred}y = \omega y$) for calculating excitations, culminating in benchmarking this against the Bose-Hubbard model.
why_interesting: This work bridges advanced algebraic geometry (variety smoothness, rank tomography) with condensed matter physics simulation. The development of PRSR offers a physically motivated refinement over standard bond dimension analysis for characterizing quantum entanglement and state structure.
